subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT gateway shutdown cancel managed active run and exec child-process scopes before the shutdown watchdog, or preserve yielded/background exec sessions unless an explicit restart or kill path is used?
rationale: Current source and release tests preserve active/background work on normal shutdown, so changing this is an operator-safety and product-policy choice rather than a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes through the supervisor before the watchdog, with documented exceptions for any background class maintainers choose to preserve.

options.title: Preserve current normal-stop behavior
options.body: Keep normal shutdown from aborting active/background exec work and treat this as a diagnostics or documentation gap unless a restart/kill path is explicitly requested.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the public session exec-control contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554 defines process ownership and termination semantics.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes through the supervisor before the watchdog, with documented exceptions for any background class maintainers choose to preserve.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current history signal across exec/process behavior and would likely own the shutdown policy tradeoff with adjacent gateway owners.
